clue.text: Broadcaster cut unserviceable operating area

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so the broadcaster word loses its tail

parts.note: US is short for unserviceable, slang for useless

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's equipment fails and its area of operation shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A radius is the range within which something works, such as a delivery service's catchment.

clue.text: With minor injuries, men are unable to stand

parts.note: ABH is actual bodily harm, the lesser assault charge in English law
OR are other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Injured soldiers cannot get to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks physical, but 'can't stand' means loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to detest it, which is what people who cannot bear something feel.

clue.text: Wearing top I keep in school study

parts.note: dressed in a vest, a top garment
to gate a pupil is to confine them to school as punishment

explanation.surface: A pupil in a vest is kept behind at school.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate is to examine closely, a verb meaning much the same as study.

clue.text: It's the same vaccination method, still

parts.note: snap is the call when two matching cards appear

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a vaccine is delivered the same way as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' reads as 'yet', but it is the noun: a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick photograph, and a still is a single photographic frame.

clue.text: Head across pond east — better fish all round

indicators.note: the two words placed all round enclose the compass point between them

explanation.surface: Fishing instructions: head east over the water to find better catches.
explanation.walkthrough: The pond is the Atlantic, so this headland is in America, in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland, and this one lies on the far side of the Atlantic, jokingly called the pond.

clue.text: Friend's twentieth anniversary

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... plate is rhyming slang for mate
second meaning: the traditional gift for twenty years of marriage

explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockney rhyming slang turns mate into china, and porcelain gifts traditionally mark twenty years of marriage.

clue.text: Stars stick with a controversial old law

parts.note: a peg is a small stick or pin
the sus law let British police stop and search on suspicion, and was repealed in 1981

explanation.surface: Celebrities hold to a disputed antique statute.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a northern constellation, a named group of stars shaped as the winged horse.

clue.text: Herbie for one was furious about one blunder a best friend spotted

parts.note: Herbie is the Volkswagen Beetle in the Love Bug films

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for being furious wraps the figure one

parts.note: raged is the past tense of rage
OG is an own goal, a football blunder

explanation.surface: The car in the films lost its temper after one of its own blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: The I sits just inside RAGED, after its first letter. A best friend is a dog, and spotted points to the Dalmatian.
explanation.definitionFit: Dalmatians were bred to run beside horse-drawn coaches, hence their old name, and dog is man's best friend.

clue.text: Casually pass dark horse with raised leg

parts.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse

indicators.note: raised in a down light means the word for leg is read from bottom to top

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A racing tip: let the outsider with a raised leg go by.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'dunno' is a colloquial way to pass on a question you cannot answer, as on a quiz show.

clue.text: Tools this waster fecklessly holds the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means the concealed run is read backwards
holds says the letters are contained inside the following words of the clue

parts.note: the run across thiS WASTER Fecklessly

explanation.surface: An idle worker holds his tools upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run reads backwards: SWASTERF turned round gives FRETSAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretsaws are fine-bladed saws for cutting curves, so they are tools.

clue.text: Smaller sport fund initially one has in reserve

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word fund

parts.note: I've is one has, with I for one

explanation.surface: A sports fund keeps money back for a rainy day.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-a-side football is a reduced version of the game with fewer players on a smaller pitch.

clue.text: Remote spot Yankee's found in going to N Ireland

indicators.note: going north in a down light means travelling upwards, so the country's name is read bottom to top
found in means the Yankee letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: An American turns up in a far corner on the way to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'N Ireland' looks like Northern Ireland, but the N goes with 'going to': north.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is an eagle's nest high on a crag, and figuratively any lofty, isolated place.

clue.text: Disparate bits in use — plus four to spare

indicators.note: being broken into disparate bits means the letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: Odd pieces in use, with four more left over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something superfluous is surplus to needs, and things to spare are extra and not needed.

clue.text: Welsh borough's auditor's being their …

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so what follows is judged by ear

parts.note: the clue runs on into the next one: being their undoing means it wrecks them

explanation.surface: A Welsh town's financial auditor is the ruin of its people.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries the sense into 18 down: something that is their undoing wrecks 'em.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrexham is a county borough and city in north-east Wales.

clue.text: Be widely involved with filling in index? The reverse?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: an index finger with something stuffed inside it
setter's reading: swap them round, so the finger is the filling inside a pastry dish

explanation.surface: Someone meddles everywhere, as if stuffing a finger.
explanation.walkthrough: The index is the forefinger; reverse filling and container and the finger goes into the pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who meddles in or is part of many different activities at once.

clue.text: Man's setting off as he pursues girl

indicators.note: pursues means comes behind, so the jumbled letters follow the girl
off suggests gone bad or out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man sets off after a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, not a male.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man sits in the stretch of sea between Great Britain and Ireland, which is its geographical setting.

clue.text: Philosopher to talk up article carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying means the article bears the small weight on its back, so it comes after

parts.note: to spin is to present favourably
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: A thinker plays up a piece of writing with little substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a seventeenth-century Dutch rationalist thinker, author of the Ethics.

clue.text: Discontinued your following something corny and crude

indicators.note: following means coming after, fixing the order of the two pieces

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your, no longer in use

explanation.surface: A dropped joke is dismissed as corny and vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests a stale joke; it is literal, a thing of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and frank about bodily matters, much as crude humour is.

clue.text: Feature otherwise put out endlessly? Not true!

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a story claiming they were expelled is false.
explanation.definitionFit: Being true can mean being loyal, so traitorous behaviour is the opposite: disloyal and faithless.

clue.text: … undoing, going with mounting resistance

indicators.note: in a down light mounting means climbing, so the resistance symbol moves up a place

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for to relieve oneself

explanation.surface: Continuing 12: the borough heads for ruin as opposition grows.
explanation.walkthrough: The R in URINATION climbs one place, above the U. The ellipsis links back to 12 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is complete destruction, the state of being undone or brought to ruin.

clue.text: Surfer enjoying a cruise?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an internet user, someone connected to the web
second meaning: split in two, aboard an ocean-going passenger ship

explanation.walkthrough: The surfer browses the internet, not the waves; the question mark flags the split reading for the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An onliner is a person using the internet, and someone on a cruise is aboard a liner.

clue.text: Compulsion's growing ultimately to broadcast celebrity feature

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are spread and resown

parts.note: taken as written, with the 's as an S

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of growing

explanation.surface: An urge grows to spread news about the famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip column is a regular newspaper section reporting on the private lives of celebrities.

clue.text: Large gas main interfered with new naval transmitter

indicators.note: things interfered with are disturbed from their arrangement

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone tampers with a big gas pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval signalman is the sailor who sends messages by flag, lamp or radio, a human transmitter.

clue.text: Sparkling wine reserved to have with dip

parts.note: cold as in aloof and distant
to duck is to dip down or under water

explanation.surface: Fizz kept back to drink with a party dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold Duck is a sweet American sparkling wine blended from champagne and red wine.

clue.text: Six go for the French test

explanation.surface: Six people sit a French exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva is an oral examination, such as a university student's spoken defence of a thesis.

clue.text: Refuse to handle — leading to trouble for dumps

indicators.note: leading to means coming first, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to black goods is to boycott them in an industrial dispute

explanation.surface: Bin workers refuse to handle rubbish, causing problems at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' and 'dumps' both suggest rubbish; dumps means low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down in the dumps is gloomy depression, which Churchill famously called his black dog.

clue.text: "Rebuked for holding bishop up" Echo tweeted

indicators.note: holding means the rebuke word wraps around what follows

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title
Echo is E in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a scolded bishop is posted online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeted' suggests social media, but it is birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: Chirruped means made short, sharp, high-pitched sounds, as a bird does when it tweets.

clue.text: Fish face being devoured by rats in east End

indicators.note: something devoured is swallowed whole, so it ends up inside

parts.note: heels are rats, and a Cockney in London's East End drops the h

explanation.surface: A sulky face is gobbled by rodents in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Heels, cads, become 'eels in the dropped-h speech of the East End, London's Cockney district.
explanation.definitionFit: Eelpouts are long, eel-like bottom-dwelling sea fish, also called viviparous blennies.

clue.text: Object to nurse running water, getting you worked up

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word cradles the other

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A patient complains about the water used in nursing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrilling event excites and stirs you, so it gets you worked up.

clue.text: Mushroom to eat: keep mum two as a starter

indicators.note: as a starter means placed first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
to take food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Dinner instructions: quietly serve a mushroom as the first course for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiitake is an edible East Asian fungus widely used in Japanese and Chinese cooking.

clue.text: Leaves unresolved job for decorator

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a task unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb; it is the noun, pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperhanging means putting up wallpaper, a standard task for a painter-and-decorator.

clue.text: Bloomer when at least three detectives prematurely ended ambush?

indicators.note: ended before its time means the final letter is lost

parts.note: a PI, private investigator, plus DIs, detective inspectors: three or more

explanation.surface: A police ambush is called off early: a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake; here it is a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy flowering houseplant, so a bloomer in the plant sense.

clue.text: Milk needing Spanish approval for one's porridge abroad

indicators.note: for one means in place of one, so the approval replaces that numeral

parts.note: a pinta is British slang for a pint of milk
ole is the Spanish cry of approval

explanation.surface: Milk for a foreign porridge needs a Spaniard's nod.
explanation.walkthrough: The I in PINTA, one, is swapped for OLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is an Italian cornmeal mush, a porridge-like dish from abroad.

clue.text: Motor part that needs wound daily

parts.note: to wing is to wound slightly
the Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A car engine part has to be wound up every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like the past of wind; it is an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing mirror is the side mirror mounted on a car's wing or door, a part of the motor.

clue.text: Make start on this puzzle? Without time to explain

indicators.note: without means outside, so the phrase goes around the time letter

parts.note: get 1 across, solve the first clue
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A solver wonders how to begin without much time.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something across is to make it understood, communicating it successfully.

clue.text: Blood group O?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's relatives, the people related by blood

definitions.note: a ring shape, hinting at the theatre tier of the same name
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the letter is ring-shaped, and the phrase also names an upper tier of seats in a theatre

explanation.walkthrough: Blood group O looks medical; read the two parts apart. The question mark flags that O only hints at a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means one's close relatives, and in theatres it is also a balcony tier, a circle shaped like the letter.

clue.text: One mocked judge, no longer on world body

parts.note: to figure is to reckon or judge

explanation.surface: A judge, ridiculed, has been dropped by an international organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of fun is a person treated as ridiculous, the butt of jokes.

clue.text: Court proceedings in which race question all but resolved

indicators.note: resolved suggests broken down and reconstituted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Q is the abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: A trial where the matter of race is nearly settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but' looks like 'nearly', but both words go into the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Racquetball is a fast game played with rackets in an enclosed court, so a match is court proceedings.

clue.text: Obsessed with old goal — a form of torture

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A fan haunted by an old goal finds it torturous.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-track mind fixes on a single subject, so the adjective describes a person fixated on one thing.

clue.text: Board ship, clutching regular selection of tackier souvenirs

parts.note: to board someone is to keep them, supplying food and lodging

indicators.note: clutching means the ship abbreviation grips the chosen letters inside it
a regular selection takes letters at even intervals from the next word

explanation.surface: Passengers board a cruise ship laden with tasteless trinkets.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepsakes are small objects kept in memory of a person or place, as souvenirs are.

clue.text: What's at the heart of propaganda, Leninist, he composed

indicators.note: at the heart of means taking the inner letters of each word

parts.note: its inner letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: Someone asks what lies at the core of communist propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the Italian violin virtuoso who wrote the famous Caprices, so a composer.

clue.text: Cold joint and a little potato

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A cold joint of meat served with a few potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a strip of fried potato, a small piece of the vegetable.

clue.text: Matter raised after hitch gets approval

indicators.note: after fixes the order, putting the matter second

parts.note: to thumb a lift is to hitchhike

indicators.note: raised in a down light means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: pus is the matter in a wound

explanation.surface: An issue comes up after a delay before getting the go-ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-up is a gesture or sign of approval and consent.

clue.text: Excitedly greet learned old author's salutation

indicators.note: doing something excitedly means agitatedly, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic welcome for a scholarly writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian novelists often addressed the audience as gentle reader, a courteous direct address.

clue.text: Deer, put in strange setting, broke out

indicators.note: a strange setting is an unfamiliar arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A deer moved to unfamiliar surroundings escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Erupted means burst forth suddenly, as a volcano or a rash does, so broke out.

clue.text: Suffer soreness, having caught illness: good thing you can drive

indicators.note: having caught means taking something inside, as a net does

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A sufferer with aches has picked up a bug, but at least can still drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach buggy is a small open off-road vehicle for driving on sand.

clue.text: Letters felt to be poorly received by Scottish bank

indicators.note: something received by another is taken into it

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish hillside or bank

explanation.surface: A letter of complaint about poor treatment by a Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money; it is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is a script of raised dots read by touch, so its characters are letters that are felt.

clue.text: Wine requirement has not exactly sunk in

indicators.note: has means contains, so the requirement holds the abbreviation within it

explanation.surface: The need for wine has not quite registered.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is a sweet wine made from the muscat grape, as in Muscat de Beaumes-de-Venise.

clue.text: Busy with pulling up weed in lake

indicators.note: pulling up in a down light means the word for busy is read from the bottom

explanation.surface: A gardener is busy pulling up weeds by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is the large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada on the California–Nevada border.

clue.text: Secretly backing America, others on the fringes in support

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the country is read backwards
in places those letters inside the word for support
on the fringes points to the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: Covert backing for America, with others on the fringes helping.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa is Latin for under the rose, an old symbol of confidentiality, and means in secret.

clue.text: Simple precis, abridged, shows up

indicators.note: up in a down light means the concealed run is read from the bottom
shows means the letters are on display within the clue words

explanation.surface: A shortened summary reveals itself as rather basic.

explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary and unsophisticated, which is what simple means here.

clue.text: House police hold in native settlement

indicators.note: in places the police abbreviation inside the other letters

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Police detain someone at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A hometown is the town where one was born or grew up, the settlement one is native to.

clue.text: Exaggerated negative impact when wife is absent

parts.note: a whammy is a blow or setback
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife's absence makes things seem worse than they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammy acting is overdone and theatrical, like a ham actor's, so exaggerated.

clue.text: Wit not contained in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is judged by how it is said

explanation.surface: A clever remark spills out uncontrolled in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright famous for epigrams, the archetypal wit.

clue.text: A moment of extreme agitation in Leicester?

annotation.spelling: TWO SHAKES OF A LAMB'S TAIL

explanation.surface: A tense moment of unrest in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is a breed of sheep as well as a city; a young one's rear end is very agitated.

clue.text: Headless corpse has finally cut down children's writer's hero

indicators.note: headless means the corpse word loses its first letter
cut down means shortened at the end

parts.note: Dr Seuss, author of The Cat in the Hat

explanation.walkthrough: The 's after writer links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus is the Greek king whose long voyage home is told in Homer's Odyssey, its central heroic figure.

clue.text: Jack in Tyne and Wear metro, perhaps, arriving at factory

Tyne and Wear is a county in North East England
RY is railway, of which a metro is an example

explanation.definitionFit: A cannery is a factory where food is preserved by sealing it in tins.

clue.text: Steal what player booked for dissent gave back?

indicators.note: gave back suggests returning, so the phrase is read in reverse

parts.words: what player booked for dissent gave
parts.note: a footballer booked for dissent gave the referee lip, cheek
